neighbours.label: words for dissipation and loss in physical systems (self-discharge, friction, viscosity, leakage, drag)
fire: Lithium cells lose a little charge each month through self-discharge.
Assume the block slides on a frictionless ramp.
Neglect the viscosity of the oil when you solve the problem.
Current leakage through the capacitor drains the circuit overnight.
Air drag slows the falling ball before it reaches the ground.
Energy dissipation in the damper turns motion into heat.
Insulation breakdown occurs when the voltage gets too high.
The orbit slowly decays as the satellite loses energy to drag.
quiet: Lithium cells store a lot of charge in a small volume.
Assume the block sits at the top of a steep ramp.
Neglect the density of the oil when you solve the problem.
Current flows through the capacitor into the circuit overnight.
Gravity pulls the falling ball down toward the ground.
Energy storage in the spring turns heat into motion.
Insulation thickness matters when the voltage gets high.
The satellite orbits the planet once every ninety minutes.
